L01 | What remains judgment is which clock and which moment the record is about, not whether to read a clock before writing a time.
L02 | What remains judgment is recognizing that calm attention was asked for, and telling presence from the extra help that was not.
L03 | What remains judgment is who counts as a different kind of reviewer, and whether the correction they offer is the one to keep.
L04 | What remains judgment is whether you have found the real cause or only a plausible name, and where an exact quote ends and your own words begin.
L05 | What remains judgment is which deliberate failure would expose a false green, and when a monitor that failed once may be trusted again.
L06 | What remains judgment is what outside source is enough to call an answer checked, and when the honest label is not checked.
L07 | What remains judgment is which test would catch a dropped warning, and whether a fact that survived the test still applies here.
L08 | What remains judgment is which remembered lesson deserves an always-step, and when that step should be changed or dropped.
L09 | What remains judgment is which code or hash is the one to copy, and whether the program copied the span that belongs in the record.
L10 | What remains judgment is which check decides, and what result is required before done or verified may be said.
L11 | What remains judgment is what an empty result, a zero, or a short list says about the search, and what may still be claimed about the world.
L12 | What remains judgment is whether the loss is real or only a wrong location or a wrong reading, and whether the remedy would destroy work that is still running.
L13 | What remains judgment is what must be inspected to see what landed, and whether that outcome matches the success that was reported.
L14 | What remains judgment is whether another source could change the answer owed, and when the places already searched are enough.
L15 | What remains judgment is which things sit beside the fix, and whether checking them shows a new break or an old one.
L16 | What remains judgment is what it would look like for the saved change to act, and whether the behavior you see was caused by that setting.
L17 | What remains judgment is how strong a claim the stated evidence can bear, and when three chats or one example are too thin to support it.
